claim: Mistral launched a public preview of Mistral Large 4 on 2026-10-06 (company announcement).
quote: Today, we’re launching a public preview of Mistral Large 4.

claim: Preview is available via API now; Mistral says weights will be released at the end of the month.
quote: You can try the preview API today on Mistral Studio. Weights drop end of this month.

claim: Mistral says ML4 has 1 trillion total parameters and 49 billion active parameters and is natively multimodal.
quote: ML4 is a 1 trillion-parameter natively multimodal model with 49 billion active parameters.

claim: Before weight release, Mistral is red-teaming the model with outside partners.
quote: Until then, we are red-teaming the model in real-world settings with cybersecurity leaders, vetted partners, and state authorities

claim: Mistral says ML4 was trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in its own datacenters.
quote: ML4 was trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral’s own datacenters

claim: Mistral says training data covered more than 160 languages.
quote: a significant share of ML4’s training data was multilingual, spanning more than 160 languages

claim: Mistral says its RL training run produces about 33 billion tokens per day at ~3k GPUs.
quote: a single training run produces roughly 33 billion tokens per day

claim: Mistral says RL training is still ongoing, expects rapid improvements, and will publish architecture/benchmarks/post-training details with the weights.
quote: We will release the weights by the end of the month, along with more details on the architecture, additional benchmarks, and our post-training methodology.

claim: Mistral argues open weights matter for cybersecurity because provider refusals can block legitimate work.
quote: provider-level refusals can block legitimate vulnerability research and incident response

claim: Mistral reports 61.7% on DeepSWE v1.1, 59.4% on SWE-Atlas-QnA, 28.3% on Terminal-Bench 4.
quote: scoring 61.7% on DeepSWE v1.1, 59.4% on SWE-Atlas-QnA, and 28.3% on Terminal-Bench 4

claim: In a blind human coding evaluation run with Surge AI, Mistral says ML4 ranked second of five, behind Claude Opus 5.
quote: ML4 Preview ranked second of five models (3.74), ahead of Kimi K3 (3.59), GLM-5.3 (3.60) and GLM-5.2 (3.40), and behind only Claude Opus 5 (4.22).

claim: Mistral claims 82% on a vulnerability reproduce-and-patch test (highest of any model) and 93% on Cybench.
quote: ML4 scores 82%, the highest of any model. It also solves 93% of the challenges in Cybench

claim: Mistral says several leading closed models (it names Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra) score near zero on that test because they refuse. Conflict of interest: this digest is written by Opus 5.5.
quote: Several leading closed models, including Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, score near zero on the same test because they refuse to perform the task.

claim: Mistral says third-party evaluator Vals AI found ML4 exceeds GPT-6-Astra on finance and legal tasks.
quote: we evaluated ML4 through third party evaluators (vals.ai) on representative tasks for both legal and financial tasks, finding the model exceeds GPT-6-Astra in both cases

claim: Mistral claims ML4's refusal rate on malicious cyber prompts is higher than all open models.
quote: the average refusal rate of the model on cyber prompts from JailbreakBench, StrongREJECT, and AgentHarm is higher than all OSS models

claim: TechCrunch (Anna Heim) covered the launch on 2026-10-06 under the headline that the 1T model aims to leapfrog closed and open rivals.
quote: Mistral’s new 1T model aims to leapfrog closed and open rivals

claim: TechCrunch reports weights are planned in about three weeks after safety testing, and quotes VP Science Pierre Stock on defensive use.
quote: Mistral plans to make its weights available in just three weeks, after safety testing is complete.

claim: Pierre Stock told TechCrunch ML4 was trained on only about 4,000 Nvidia GPUs (vs 3,800 in Mistral's post).
quote: ML4 was trained entirely on Mistral’s compute; using only 4,000 Nvidia GPUs

claim: TechCrunch reports Mistral hopes (benchmarks pending at time of interview) ML4 will be best in class among open-weight models and could beat closed models in specific areas.
quote: Thanks to focused training, it could also outperform closed models in specific areas that are key to its customers

claim: Artificial Analysis independently scores the ML4 preview at 38 on its Intelligence Index, above the price-tier median of 26.
quote: Mistral Large 4 Preview scores 38 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, placing it above average among other reasoning models in a similar price tier (median: 26).

claim: Artificial Analysis lists pricing of $1.36/M input and $4.18/M output tokens and a 524k context window.
quote: $1.36 per 1M input tokens

claim: Artificial Analysis found ML4 very verbose: 200M tokens to run its index vs median 81M.
quote: it generated 200M tokens, which is very verbose in comparison to the median of 81M.

claim: Vals AI ranks ML4 #32 of 44 on the Vals Index (48.05%); its best result is #6 of 75 on Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark.
quote: It ranks #32 of 44 models on the Vals Index with 48.05%. Its best result is #6 of 75 on Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark

claim: Vals AI lists ML4 at 54.68% (22/75) on Finance Agent v2 and 22.73% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (vs Mistral's self-reported 28.3%).
quote: Finance Agent (v2) 54.68 % ± 0.58 22 / 75 ... Terminal-Bench 4.0 22.73

claim: Mistral's product card describes ML4 as an open-weight hybrid instruct-and-reasoning MoE with multimodal input.
quote: Open-weight hybrid instruct-and-reasoning MoE with multimodal input

claim: Mistral's listed price is $1.36 per million input tokens and $4.18 per million output tokens.
quote: Input (/M tokens) $1.36 Output (/M tokens) $4.18

claim: Simon Willison summarizes the release: 1T params, 49B active, 3,800 GPUs, preview via API, open weights promised end of month.
quote: Today they're releasing a preview of Mistral Large 4, a 1 trillion parameter, 49 billion active parameter model trained on their own cluster of 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs.

claim: Simon Willison assesses ML4 as about six months behind the frontier and notes only two reasoning levels.
quote: It's certainly not a Fable-class model, but it's great to see Mistral put out a model that's back to being maybe about 6 months behind the frontier.

claim: Per Simon Willison, ML4's AA score of 38 is a big jump from Mistral Large 3's score of 9.
quote: It's a huge improvement on last December's Mistral Large 3, which drew this terrible pelican and scored 9 on AA.

claim: The HN thread 'Mistral Large 4' reached 1,552 points; simonw noted only 'none' and 'high' reasoning settings.
quote: Surprisingly it only supports reasoning "none" or reasoning "high".

claim: A top HN comment praised vision and cyber benchmarks.
quote: Impressive vision benchmarking.

claim: A highly-replied HN comment called the model mediocre and late.
quote: This model doesn’t knock anybody’s socks off. The model is (and I hate to be this harsh) mediocre, and this mediocrity has also arrived months late.

claim: An HN commenter questioned pricing vs cheaper open models with similar capability.
quote: Seems hard to get customers at that price range when you're competing with open source models that are 1/2 - 1/3 the price but with similar capabilities.

claim: An HN commenter noted the 'Frontier performance' framing lacks an Opus 5.5 comparison.
quote: >Frontier performance * proceeds to not compare to Opus 5.5
